<run>
<cmdlet>
<object>

For each (address, user) with an interactive credential failure from the address (a code of the credential_failure_codes list, stored in case_meta; a sign-in of unknown kind counts as interactive), the user is EXCUSED only if they have a known success (error_code 0) from that address either BEFORE their first credential failure there (the address was already theirs) or within 30 minutes AFTER one of their failures there (a typo correction). Every other failed user is a SPRAYED user, including users whose only successes there come later (the takeover pattern). An address is a source when at least 5 users were sprayed AND the sprayed users outnumber the excusing users (distinct users with a known success from the address, minus the late-takeover users). An office NAT or VPN egress, where users mistype and succeed within minutes or have signed in for days, is not a source; a proxy that sprays and takes accounts over stays one. The address type does not matter and no GeoIP is needed. Rules read it through the tenant scope like any tenant-aware table; cloud_services reads it to disqualify a pair whose users were sprayed.

name: state_absent_in_newer
comment: State rows a newer capture of the same artifact, for the same subject and tenant, no longer holds. Latest-wins (Phase 2b) never deletes, so a row removed between two captures (e.g. an inbox rule) otherwise still reads as current; this view lists it instead. Rule: same artifact_type, same subject (case-insensitively), same tenant_key, a collection exists for that (artifact_type, subject, tenant_key) that sparrow_collection_is_newer than the record's last-seen collection and whose files do not hold the record. sparrow_collection_is_newer(x, y) is exactly ingest/state.rs update_existing's rule: compare collected_at when both x and y have one, else compare collection_id - never mixing the two, so an unknown collected_at is not "very old", it simply makes the comparison fall back to collection_id entirely, on both sides. That relation is well-defined for any two collections directly but is not a total order across 3+ with mixed known/unknown collected_at (it can cycle), so "last seen" and "absent from" are each picked by ranking every candidate by how many other candidates in the same comparison beat it (ascending; 0 for an outright winner, tied but never all beaten inside a cycle) with collection_id descending as the deterministic tie-break - never by sorting on one derived key, and never by keeping only an unbeaten row (which a cycle can leave empty). A byte-identical newer file (duplicate_file) counts as holding whatever its parsed twin (same sha256, artifact_type and, case-insensitively, subject) holds, mirroring the ingest dedup check in ingest/mod.rs. A subject not collected at all in the newer capture (no file for it) yields no later file to compare against, so its rows are not listed - coverage gaps are not the same as removal. transport_rules and remote_domains rows are keyed per collection (<collection_id>|<name>); they are matched across captures on the name without that prefix (macro sparrow_state_match_key), so a transport rule or remote domain a newer capture of the tenant no longer holds is listed here, keyed by the row of its last sighting. "Last seen" and "absent from" are ranked within the record's own tenant: another tenant's capture never hides or reports a removal.
